blocks.title: Proposal: idea, worksheet, papers
blocks.note:
Proposal due Wed 4pm.
1. Jot 3 ideas for a repeated-measures variable that could change mind-wandering, then pick one (15 min)
2. Fill in the worksheet: idea, hypotheses, conditions, measure (20 min)
3. Find 2 more papers that back up your idea (25 min)

blocks.title: Proposal: write the Introduction
blocks.note: Write the Introduction, ending with your hypotheses (25 min, keep going if it flows)

blocks.title: Proposal: Method and expected results
blocks.note:
1. Write the Method in future tense: participants, design, materials, procedure (25 min)
2. Write the expected results and why they would matter (20 min)

blocks.title: Proposal: check against the criteria
blocks.note: Check it against the marking criteria and tidy APA references (20 min). Save it ready to submit.

blocks.title: Submit the proposal (due 4pm)
blocks.note:
1. Read it once out loud and fix anything that sounds off (15 min)
2. Check the word count (1,500) and submit on Canvas (5 min)
Then you're done. Rest of the block is yours.

blocks.title: Dev Psych essay: question and readings
blocks.note:
1. Read the three essay questions and pick one (5 min)
2. Open the matching seminar page and note its two essential readings (5 min)
3. Read the first essential reading, abstract then conclusion (15 min)
4. Read the second essential reading the same way (15 min)

blocks.title: Dev Psych plan, quick look at the rest
blocks.note:
1. Dev Psych: write your one-sentence answer to the question (5 min)
2. Dev Psych: find 2 more studies on the reading list, one for and one against (25 min)
3. Dev Psych: bullet-point plan: intro, 3 points with evidence, conclusion (20 min)
4. Stats report: open Lab Report Information and read only Coding & Analysis (5 min)
5. Poster: find which question you were given (5 min)
